questions.stem: At a life-cycle cost comparison, a supervisor proposes: "Continue the ineffective concept until the $80,000 is recovered". The underlying case is: A project has already spent $80,000 on a control concept that now appears ineffective. A better alternative costs $40,000 from today forward. How should the prior spending influence the decision? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Select the original concept because changing direction admits a management error
Add the sunk cost only to the new alternative to make comparison fair
Treat the $80,000 as sunk and compare the future costs, benefits, and risks of the available options
Continue the ineffective concept until the $80,000 is recovered
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Costs already incurred and unrecoverable should not distort a forward-looking decision. The choice should be based on incremental future consequences.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Select the original concept because changing direction admits a management error' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sunk costs principle.
The proposed response 'Add the sunk cost only to the new alternative to make comparison fair' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sunk costs principle.
The proposed response 'Continue the ineffective concept until the $80,000 is recovered' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sunk costs principle.
